wps.title: Step-up authentication for account-takeover tooling, notices to the target, consented support access
wps.brief:
Close S-06 (= SEC L-7). Read the S-06 entry in docs/build/REGISTER-2026-11-05.md first (its verified smallest fix names the functions and lines; line numbers may have shifted since wave A — grep the function names).
DECISIONS TAKEN (the owner delegated them): (a) Move the password check from src/server/actions/profile.ts into src/server/auth/password.ts as verifyUserPassword(userId, password) and use it from both places (wave A added a change-password action in profile.ts — keep it working). (b) Step-up: resetTwoFactorAction, createLinkAction for kind 'reset' (invite links for never-activated accounts stay as they are), the role change in updatePersonAction (only when the role actually changes) and the operator's adminLinkAction in platform.ts take a `password` argument; first thing after actionViewer: a per-ACTOR rate limit `step-up:${v.user.id}` of 10 per 15 minutes and verifyUserPassword; failure returns { ok: false, error: 'wrongPassword' } (and 'rateLimited' when limited), audited as 'security.step_up_failed'. (c) Notices: the target always gets an in-app notice plus an email through notifyUsers with a new FIXED_MESSAGES kind (one per action: twoFactorReset, resetLinkIssued, roleChanged); when the target is a tenant_admin, every other active tenant_admin of the organisation also gets the in-app notice (peer-administrator action). A second-approver queue is NOT built: return in your summary a short ADR paragraph that records why (step-up + notices + audit, approver queue is a policy question for the owner). (d) Operator reset link becomes a consented support grant: TenantSettings.security.supportAccessUntil (ISO string | null, type-only change in schema.ts/tenant-defaults.ts withDefaults); a tenant administrator grants 72 hours from Settings → Security (button 'Allow Safarov Industries support access for 72 hours' + 'Revoke'; audit 'support.access_granted' / 'support.access_revoked'); adminLinkAction refuses with error 'supportAccess' unless now < supportAccessUntil, and the operator console shows the grant state per organisation. (e) UI: the confirm dialogs in person-actions.tsx, people-client.tsx and platform-client.tsx gain a password field (copy the profile password field; autocomplete current-password; accessible label), ten locales for every new string. Keep every existing audit() entry and lockout semantics. Tests: step-up refused with wrong password and after 10 failures, accepted with the right one; notices written to the target and to peer admins; operator link refused without a grant, accepted inside the 72 h, refused after revoke; role change without role change needs no password.
acceptance: 2FA reset, reset link, role change and the operator reset link require the actor's password, rate limited per actor (tests)
The target and, for a tenant_admin target, every other administrator are notified; audit entries exist for success and failure (tests)
Operator reset links work only inside a tenant-granted 72-hour support window (tests); the grant and revoke are audited and visible in Settings → Security and in /super
All new strings in ten locales with key parity; dialogs accessible; typecheck, lint and the touched tests pass; nothing under portal/drizzle committed

wps.title: Key versioning and rotation for APP_SECRET, stable domain-proof key, unique verified tenant domains
wps.brief:
Close S-07 and S-11 (b). Read both register entries first (S-07's smallest fix is the design: one previous key, kid routing, v1 compatibility, rotate script, runbook).
DECISIONS TAKEN: (a) env.ts: optional APP_SECRET_PREVIOUS (min 32 chars) and optional APP_DOMAIN_PROOF_SECRET (default: APP_SECRET, documented 'set it once and never rotate it'). (b) crypto.ts: keys() = [current, previous?]; kid = sha256(secret).slice(0, 8); encryptSecret writes 'v2:<kid>:<iv>:<tag>:<data>'; decryptSecret routes v2 by kid and tries every key for v1 — the v1 path must stay byte-identical and is pinned by a fixture ciphertext in tests/crypto.test.ts. (c) TOTP backup codes: hashed with the current key, verification also accepts the previous-key hash (same pattern as the existing legacy hash loop in actions/auth.ts). (d) Domain proof: the TXT value derives from the domain-proof secret only; during a rotation every check (settings verifyDomainAction, platform verifyTenantDomainAction, the jobs.ts re-check) accepts the value derived from either key; existing TXT records keep verifying (fixture). (e) scripts/rotate-secret.ts: re-encrypts every tenants.settings *Enc field and users.totp_secret with the current key (decrypting with any key), idempotent, prints counts only, refuses to run with a dev-only secret in production; tests run it on the in-memory PGlite. (f) Signed values (cookies, links) are not re-signed: old ones become invalid after rotation — state it in the runbook. (g) S-11 (b): partial unique index tenants_domain_verified_idx on tenants(domain) where domain_verified_at is not null (schema.ts only, no committed migration); verifyDomainAction and verifyTenantDomainAction catch isUniqueViolation(error, 'tenants_domain_verified_idx') and return 'domainTaken' (ten locales, admin settings and platform namespaces); check scripts/seed-data.ts so the seed never creates two verified tenants with one domain. (h) Runbook: docs/OPERATIONS.md gets a 'Rotating APP_SECRET' section (four steps) and portal/README.md operations notes link to it; .env.example documents the two new variables. Tests: v1 fixture decrypts, v2 kid routing, wrong kid falls back, rotate script on an in-memory DB, backup code accepted under the previous key, domain proof accepted under either key, second verified tenant with the same domain refused.
acceptance: Ciphertexts written before the change still decrypt (fixture test); new ciphertexts carry a key id; a rotation with APP_SECRET_PREVIOUS set keeps mail/SMS/webhook secrets, TOTP backup codes and domain proofs working (tests)
scripts/rotate-secret.ts re-encrypts every stored secret and is idempotent (test)
A second organisation cannot verify a domain another organisation has already verified; the message exists in ten locales (test)
Runbook present in docs/OPERATIONS.md; .env.example documents APP_SECRET_PREVIOUS and APP_DOMAIN_PROOF_SECRET; typecheck, lint, touched tests pass; nothing under portal/drizzle committed

wps.title: Generated cross-tenant and lower-role test suite, RLS evaluation, tutor cache per tenant, lessonKey and sign-off IP hardening
wps.brief:
Close S-03 (test suite + RLS evaluation), S-10, S-11 (c) and S-11 (d). Read those register entries first.
DECISIONS TAKEN: (a) S-03: write portal/scripts/inventory-surface.ts that lists every exported function of portal/src/server/actions/*.ts and every exported HTTP method of portal/src/app/api/**/route.ts together with the guard it calls (actionViewer/apiViewer/getViewer permission string, or 'public'); commit its output as portal/tests/fixtures/surface.json. Write portal/tests/cross-tenant.test.ts, table-driven on tests/helpers/db.ts: two organisations A and B with an administrator viewer each plus a learner viewer, and for EVERY tenant-scoped action and route in the inventory a row that calls it as A with B's ids/tokens/slugs (and as the learner where a permission is required) and asserts refusal ({ ok:false } / 403 / 404 / empty) AND that no row of B changed (snapshot B's relevant tables before and after). A test fails when surface.json and the live inventory differ (so a new action cannot be added without a row) and when an inventory entry has no row in the table. Fix any real leak you find (each fix gets its own commit and a note in your summary). (b) RLS: do NOT implement; write (in your summary, for the ADR) a concrete evaluation: what PostgreSQL RLS with SET LOCAL app.tenant_id per transaction would take given src/server/db's module-level db() singleton, PGlite in tests, the non-owner role in docker-compose, the 34 tenant tables, and your verdict on whether the suite satisfies due diligence; the owner question goes to left_open. (c) S-10: src/app/api/tutor/route.ts cache key prefixed with the tenant id (wave A already added the lesson-text hash — keep it) and a test that the same question from two organisations produces two tutor_cache rows; the clean-up of old rows already exists in jobs.ts (365 days). (d) S-11 (c): learning.ts touch/start-lesson actions verify lessonKey belongs to the module (query, mirrors completeLessonAction) and cap the string; test. (e) S-11 (d): the policy sign-off CSV route emits the IP column only for roles with audit.read (can() from src/server/auth/permissions.ts); test both roles.
acceptance: tests/cross-tenant.test.ts covers every tenant-scoped action and route handler (inventory-checked) with another organisation's ids and a lower role; all refuse and nothing of the other organisation changes
Any real cross-tenant or role leak found is fixed with a regression test and listed in the summary
Tutor cache rows are per organisation (test); lessonKey validated (test); sign-off IPs only for audit.read roles (test)
RLS evaluation written for the ADR; typecheck, lint, touched tests pass

wps.title: Click counted by beacon, simulation sender address with domain proof, delivery allow-listing guide, image digests
wps.brief:
Close M-09 (a)(b)(c) and I-4. Read the M-09 and I-4 register entries first. The live drill (src/server/services/drill.ts) calls recordClick directly and must keep working.
DECISIONS TAKEN: (a) A click is counted only after a JavaScript beacon: new simulationClickAction(token, via) in src/server/actions/campaigns.ts (token /^[a-z2-7]{10,40}$/, isLikelyScanner() refused, then recordClick) called once on mount by components/site/teachable.tsx before the fake sign-in shows; the /t/[token] and /q/[token] page renders no longer record a click (tracking view peeks only); /q passes via 'qr'; opens (pixel) unchanged. Update tests/simulation-tracking.test.ts: a GET render with a browser user agent records nothing, the action records once, a second call is idempotent, a scanner UA is refused. (b) email.simulationFromAddress in TenantSettings (type-only), a field in Settings → Email with ten-locale label/hint, zod in actions/settings.ts; the address's domain must be proven: reuse the existing domain-proof helpers (a second TXT record for that domain, same derivation, shown next to the field with a Verify button) and refuse to save an unproven domain; mail.ts uses it as the From address only for kind 'simulation'. (c) docs/SIMULATION-DELIVERY.md: step-by-step allow-listing for Microsoft 365 (Defender advanced delivery → third-party phishing simulation: sender domains, IPs, the simulation URL) and Google Workspace (inbound gateway / spam allow-list by sender and IP), SPF/DKIM for the sending domain, what the scanner detection does and does not catch, and a note that the look-alike domain itself is the owner's choice (register has it as owner item). (d) I-4: pin portal/Dockerfile's base image by its multi-arch index digest and postgres:16-alpine in both compose files; read the digests from the registry with curl (anonymous token: GET https://auth.docker.io/token?service=registry.docker.io&scope=repository:library/node:pull, then GET https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/library/node/manifests/24-trixie-slim with Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json, application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json; the Docker-Content-Digest header is the index digest) and verify the digest is an index, not a single-platform manifest; reword portal/README.md's '--pull' sentence to 'Dependabot proposes the digest bump weekly'. If the registry is unreachable, leave the tag and say so in left_open.
acceptance: A mail scanner fetching the landing page never counts as a click; a real browser counts exactly once through the beacon; QR landings count with via 'qr'; the live drill still records clicks (tests)
A simulation sender address can be set only for a proven domain and is used only for simulation mail (tests)
docs/SIMULATION-DELIVERY.md exists and is linked from docs/API.md or portal/README.md
Dockerfile and compose images pinned by index digest (or left_open explains why not); typecheck, lint, touched tests pass; nothing under portal/drizzle committed

DECISIONS TAKEN: TenantSettings.retention = { auditMonths: number; learningMonths: number } with 0 = keep forever (default); jobs.ts cleanup() loops tenants inside the existing deadline/deleteInBatches budget and deletes, per tenant with a non-zero value, audit_log rows older than auditMonths and answers + behavior_risks rows older than learningMonths; lesson_progress, xp_events, attestations and certificates are never deleted (compliance evidence). Two number inputs (0–120) in Settings → Security (or where the privacy settings live) with ten-locale labels and a hint that 0 keeps everything; zod in actions/settings.ts; audit 'settings.updated' as the other settings do. docs/OPERATIONS.md gets a 'Data retention and residency' section: what the job deletes, the fixed platform retentions (demo requests 24 months, tutor cache 12 months, sessions), and residency as a hosting decision (the owner's region answer is an open question — do not invent a region). Tests: extend tests/jobs-runner.test.ts (or the jobs test file that exists): one tenant with auditMonths 1 and an old audit row is cleaned, a tenant with 0 keeps its rows, the other tenant's rows are untouched, lesson_progress untouched.
acceptance: Retention settings saved per organisation, default keep, validated (test)
Clean-up deletes only what the organisation configured, inside the time budget, never evidence tables, never another organisation's rows (tests)
Ten-locale strings with parity; docs/OPERATIONS.md section present; typecheck, lint, touched tests pass

wps.brief:

DESIGN: (1) Route GET /api/admin/modules/[id]/scorm?locale=<one of the ten> (apiViewer with the studio or reports permission that fits the existing permission table; module must be reachable by the tenant: library or own) streams a zip built with the zip writer already in src/server/reports/xlsx.ts (move it to src/server/zip.ts and reuse it there). (2) Package: imsmanifest.xml for SCORM 1.2 (one organization, one SCO item per module, adlcp:masteryscore when the module has scored scenes, the resources list), launcher.html, player.js + player.css (the offline bundle), lessons.json (every lesson of the module in the chosen locale from lesson_contents, falling back to en), and assets the scenes reference if any. (3) Offline bundle: portal/scripts/build-scorm-player.ts bundles a small entry (src/scorm/entry.tsx) with esbuild (already in node_modules as a transitive dependency of tsx — import it directly; if it is not resolvable say so in left_open instead of installing) that renders the existing player components (components/player) with NextIntlClientProvider from next-intl and the ten message bundles the player needs, Tailwind CSS compiled for the bundle with the @tailwindcss/postcss or @tailwindcss/node API already installed, no server actions: the player gets a progress sink prop (add an optional `onProgress`/`onComplete` to player.tsx that replaces the server-action calls when present) which the entry wires to the SCORM 1.2 API adapter (LMSInitialize, LMSSetValue cmi.core.lesson_status 'completed'/'passed'/'failed', cmi.core.score.raw from src/lib/content/scoring.ts run in the browser, cmi.core.session_time, LMSCommit, LMSFinish) found by the standard window/parent/opener walk. Narration: Web Speech fallback only; AI Sel tutor: disabled in the package (the scene shows the lesson text). The built bundle is NOT committed: the route builds it on demand on first use and caches it under .data/scorm/ (or portal builds it in the Dockerfile builder stage — choose the simpler that works in both dev and the image; document). (4) Admin UI: an 'Export SCORM 1.2' button with a locale picker on the module page in the admin catalog/studio, ten locales for the strings; audit 'module.exported'. (5) Tests: manifest generated for a seeded module validates against the SCORM 1.2 manifest rules you encode in the test (required elements, identifiers unique, every resource file present in the zip), the zip lists every file, the entry's API-adapter wiring is tested with a fake API object (status and score set on completion), and a vitest renders one scene of each type through the offline entry without a server. Keep the package self-contained: opening launcher.html from a file:// LMS harness must work (no absolute URLs).

The offline player renders every scene type without the server and reports completion and score through the SCORM API (test with a fake API)
